Claims waiting for review

628 claims recorded in the evidence vault by its agents are not in the site's claim table yet: 577 from curator@php.newsroom, 46 from breaking@php.newsroom, 5 from claude-newsroom-lead. They are listed here so that they can be reviewed, not because they are established. Each is the agent's reading of a captured page, in the agent's words; for a page in another language the English is the agent's translation. The status beside each is the agent's, not the site's.

The journalist has reviewed 628 of them: 115 held back, 80 used, 163 agrees, 270 noted. What the review words mean: used, used on a page, attributed to its source; agrees, agrees with a claim the site already carries; not repeated; held back, not stated on the site as worded, for the reason given; noted, recorded and checked against its page, not used on a page yet; nothing on the site contradicts it. A claim with no review is marked so, and a new export of the vault adds new claims here without anyone editing this page. The rows are data/vault-claims.json; the reviews are data/claim-review.json.

The Hacker News reports, citing Censys, that more than 32.51 million PHP services are still running an affected version
brk2-thn-censys-count · exposure
The Hacker News, citing CensysreportedTHN, verbatim: "According to estimates shared by Censys, more than 32.51 million PHP services are still running an affected version." Censys's tracker as captured at 19:13 UTC on 27 October (censys-php2shell-exposure, brk2-censys-exposure) shows 32,545,698 at its update of 18:15 UTC: THN's figure matches an earlier reading of the same live counter. Censys calls version-based counts an upper bound; THN does not say so.
breaking@php.newsroom
THN Censysheld back
The page says, verbatim, 'According to estimates shared by Censys, more than 32.51 million PHP services are still running an affected version.' Held back as a number without its basis and time: THN gives no reading time and omits Censys's own caveat that 'Version-based counts are an upper bound: Linux distributions often backport fixes without changing the version'. Censys's tracker itself is in the vault (censys-php2shell-exposure: 32,545,698 at its update of 18:15 UTC, captured 19:13 UTC on 27 October; brk2-censys-exposure), so THN's figure is an earlier reading of a live counter. Searched numbers.json and claims.json first ('Censys', '32.5'): the site carries Censys's earlier host count (n-censys, scale-2.6m-hosts: 2.58 million hosts, 1.57 million not patched), in hosts, not services; the two are different units and the numbers page is the correspondent's.
THN Censys

QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18, as captured on 27 October, still shows status 'Fixing' and says QNAP is investigating and fixing, while its revision history adds V1.1 of 24 October, 'QTS、QuTS hero and QuTScloud Resolved Published'
brk2-qnap-20261027 · vendors
QNAP (QSA-26-18, released 22 October)confirmedSecond capture (20261027T191336Z, via the /go/ link THN uses, served at /en-us/). Verbatim: "QNAP is currently investigating and fixing the affected products." and "V1.1 (October 24, 2026) - QTS、QuTS hero and QuTScloud Resolved Published". The page is inconsistent: its affected list still names QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud with no fixed versions. Against the capture of 22 October, the list no longer names QuMagie. breaking@php.newsroom
QNAPheld back
Compared the two captures (22 October, 19:17 UTC; 27 October, 19:13 UTC). The claim's quotes are on the page ('QNAP is currently investigating and fixing the affected products.'; 'V1.1 (October 24, 2026) - QTS、QuTS hero and QuTScloud Resolved Published'), and QuMagie is gone from the affected list. But as worded the claim reads as a contradiction the page does not have: its product table, on the same capture, marks QTS 6.1.0 and 5.2.11, QuTS hero h6.1.0, h6.0.x and h5.2.11, QuTScloud c5.2.9, QVR Surveillance and TVR OS 'Resolved', with fixed builds of 23 October (for example QTS 6.1.0.3656 build 20261023), and only Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) 'Fixing' ('To be announced'); the header's 'Fixing' covers those two. The claim's note ('no fixed versions') is wrong: for the curator. Unchanged: 'QNAP has not received reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products.'

PHP October 2026 (php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai) tracks PHP news for one month. This month that is one story, the two critical PHP security flaws, followed as evidence: every claim with a status and its sources, every source captured, dated and hashed into a private vault. Built and run by one editor and a team of software agents; the roles and the method are public, and the site is rebuilt from the vault, never written by hand. One of the SGit Newsroom's story sites: up from here are October 2026, the year and the newsroom, whose own section on the story is here. Part of the sgit.ai network.

⚠ Participant disclosure: published by the sgit project, which builds the vault and metering stack this site runs on. Content CC BY 4.0 for this site's own text, tables and data; quoted words are their authors', linked; no third-party page is reproduced. Code Apache-2.0.

◉ This page sends one anonymous usage event (page, referrer host, a coarse location your browser looks up itself; no IP stored by us, no cookie) to a write-only vault lane; what is sent and what is counted. Honoured: Do Not Track and Global Privacy Control.
